title: 03 — Sync, uploads, realtime
tagline: How the backend keeps devices in step, accepts files and reports their state. Request and response shapes: 01-api.

blocks.html:
1.1 Revisions

  • Each user has one counter, sync_state.last_rev. Every row a push writes gets the next number in rev.
  • A push first locks the user's sync_state row (select … for update). A second push of the same user waits, so revs are committed in order.
Why not a timestamp or a sequenceWhat goes wrong
updated_at > sinceTwo devices' clocks differ; a row written "in the past" is never pulled
nextval() sequenceRev 8 can commit before rev 7; a device that pulled up to 8 never sees 7

1.2 Pull

  • Revs are unique per user, so limit + 1 rows from each table are enough to find the first limit overall.

1.3 Push

CaseResult
New rowapplied
Existing row, mutation newerapplied (frozen columns keep their value; sessions.state takes the higher state)
Existing row, mutation oldersuperseded + stored row (unless sessions.state moved forward: then applied)
Row deleted on the serversuperseded + tombstone
Same natural key as a live rowsuperseded + that row
Id owned by another userrejected: forbidden
Bad value or broken rulerejected: invalid_row:<code>; the rest of the batch still applies
Parent missing at commitBatch retried one mutation per transaction; only that one rejected: missing_parent
  • Last write wins is decided in SQL: where t.client_updated_at < excluded.client_updated_at.
  • A delete wins a tie with an edit made at the same millisecond.

  • Reading objects back from EC2 in the same region costs nothing.

blocks.html:
• The notification carries ids only (Postgres caps payloads at 8000 bytes); the hub reads the row.
  • pg_notify inside a transaction is delivered at commit and dropped on rollback.
  • Delivery is at most once. The snapshot after every subscribe is how the app catches up.
  • Works unchanged with one API process or several.

Diagram: complete / abort, (API) → pg_notify upload_events, {uid, sessionId, uploadId, type} → Postgres → verify worker → pg_notify → LISTEN → RealtimeHub, in each API process → re-read row → jobCompleted / jobFailed → app sockets of that uid,, subscribed to that session

blocks.html:
JobWhenDoes
VerifyContinuously, one upload at a timeClaims the oldest registered upload (for update skip locked, a 30-minute claim), hashes it, sets verified or mismatch, notifies; F16: pushes when a session is fully verified
Abandoned uploadsHourlycreated uploads older than 7 days → abort in S3, aborted
Tombstone purgeDailyDeletes rows with deleted_at older than 90 days, raises purged_through_rev
  • S3 also deletes unfinished multipart parts after 7 days (bucket lifecycle rule).
